prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a side impact at intersection in Conroe, Texas, and has neck strain. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1253; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thanks for taking the time to speak with me today. This recorded statement concerns the collision you reported at an intersection in Conroe, Texas. Please state your full name for the record.

A: Sure. I'd rather keep my name off the recording, if that's all right. I'm the driver of the blue sedan that was involved.

Q: That works. Can you describe where you were coming from and where you were headed when the collision happened?

A: I was driving through the intersection on the main road, heading straight through. The light had been green for a bit when I started into it.

Q: Did you see the other vehicle before the impact?

A: Not really. It came in from my right side, and I only saw it a split second before it hit me on the passenger door.

Q: How fast would you estimate you were going?

A: Maybe around the posted limit, nothing unusual. I wasn't in a hurry.

Q: After the impact, did you notice any injuries right away?

A: My neck was stiff and sore almost immediately. I didn't think much of it at the scene, but by the next morning I had a lot of tightness and some pain running into my shoulders.

Q: Have you seen a medical provider since the collision?

A: Yes, I went to an urgent care clinic and then I've been following up with my family doctor. They diagnosed me with a neck strain and gave me muscle relaxers and a referral for physical therapy.

Q: Are you still experiencing symptoms today?

A: Yes, I still get stiffness when I turn my head, and sitting for long drives is harder than it used to be.

Q: Is there anything else you'd like to add to your statement?

A: Only that I've been trying to keep up with my appointments and I'm hoping to get back to normal soon.

Q: Thank you. This concludes the statement.
